idea.body: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. Its opposite sides are always equal, and its opposite angles are always equal too. Two angles next to each other, like the top and the side, always add to 180 degrees. A robot's solar panel frame is a parallelogram with one angle of 65 degrees. Its opposite angle is also 65 degrees, and each angle next to it is 180 minus 65, which is 115 degrees. A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal, and its diagonals always cross at a right angle. A kite is different. Its two pairs of equal sides sit next to each other, not across from each other. Its diagonals still cross at a right angle.

figure.alt: A parallelogram with a 65 degree angle, its opposite angle also 65 degrees, and the two other angles each 115 degrees.

workedExample.prompt: A kite-shaped drone frame has two pairs of consecutive equal sides. One pair is 8 centimeters each, and the other pair is 13 centimeters each. What is the frame's perimeter?
steps: A kite has two pairs of sides that are equal, each pair next to each other.
The perimeter adds all four sides together.
8 + 8 is 16, and 13 + 13 is 26, so the total is 16 + 26, which is 42 centimeters.

figure.alt: A kite with two short sides of 8 centimeters meeting at the top vertex. Its two long sides of 13 centimeters meet at the bottom vertex.

ways.name: The property checklist
ways.when: Use this when you know one angle or side of a parallelogram, rhombus or kite.
steps: A solar panel frame is a parallelogram with one angle of 72 degrees.
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are always equal.
Angles next to each other always add up to 180 degrees.
The angle next to the 72 degree angle is 180 minus 72, which is 108 degrees.
The angle opposite that 108 degree angle is also 108 degrees.
ways.example: A parallelogram has one angle of 72 degrees. Find the angle across the frame from it, on the near side.
ways.trap: Assuming all four angles are equal instead of only the opposite pair.

figure.alt: A parallelogram with angles 108, 72, 108 and an unknown angle at the fourth corner. Single ticks mark one pair of equal sides, double ticks mark the other pair.

frames.caption: One angle of the frame is 72 degrees

ways.name: The diagonals test
ways.when: Use this when you know how a quadrilateral's diagonals cross but not its side lengths.
steps: A frame's diagonals bisect each other and cross at a right angle, but are not equal in length.
Diagonals that bisect each other always mean the shape is a parallelogram.
Diagonals that also cross at a right angle mean it is a rhombus.
Equal diagonals would make it a square instead, but these are not equal.
So this quadrilateral is a rhombus.
ways.example: A quadrilateral's diagonals bisect each other and cross at a right angle, but are not equal. Name it.
ways.trap: Calling it a square just because the diagonals are perpendicular, without checking they are also equal.

figure.alt: A rhombus with dashed diagonals crossing at a right angle at the center. All four sides carry a single tick mark.

frames.caption: Diagonals bisect each other, cross at a right angle.
Diagonals bisect, cross at right angle, unequal
Equal diagonals would mean a square instead
So this quadrilateral is a rhombus

ways.name: Coordinates and slopes
ways.when: Use this when a quadrilateral's corners are given as coordinates.
steps: A frame has corners at (0, 0), (4, 2), (6, 6) and (2, 4).
Opposite sides of a parallelogram must have the same slope.
The side from (0, 0) to (4, 2) has slope 2/4, which is 1/2.
The side from (2, 4) to (6, 6) has slope (6 - 4)/(6 - 2), which is also 1/2.
Both pairs of opposite sides match, so it is a parallelogram.
ways.example: A quadrilateral has corners (0, 0), (4, 2), (6, 6) and (2, 4). Is it a parallelogram?
ways.answer: Yes, both pairs of opposite sides have equal slopes
ways.trap: Comparing two adjacent sides instead of a pair of opposite sides, which are the ones expected to match.
